correctness.rationale: For two equal m-point blocks, quotient-bijective transformations are all regular: each block-restriction has a right inverse. When both blocks map into the same target class, a preserving right inverse exists iff one input-block image contains the other; preimages of the whole target class cannot be distributed among two inverse-image blocks. Given target image rank r, inclusion–exclusion on the two possible nested image containments gives C_r=4 binom(m,r)(r!S(m,r))r^m−2 binom(m,r)(r!S(m,r))². Independent class-bijective maps yield 2P_m(z)². Sangkhanan full-text §3 definitions reduce M1 to quotient-bijective maps plus 2m constants and M2 to common-target regular maps plus 2(m!)² units, with intersection constants + units. Exact rank polynomials follow. E image size ≤3m/4; one-coordinate bounded differences imply Pr(K>7m/8)≤e^(−m/32), giving exponential small nested-image probability and specified asymptotic fractions. Endpoints m=2 and all r are covered. Independent original-map enumeration and literal inverse search at m=2,3 reproduce all rank coefficients; these finite checks do not establish m unbounded.

value.rationale: The two maximal unit-containing regular subsemigroups form a natural, already classified pair in finite transformation semigroup theory. Exact labeled rank distributions, their intersection and the striking exponentially divergent asymptotic volumes resolve a genuine quantitative gap, adding more than a textbook restatement of maximality. The full rank enumeration is useful for random maps and semigroup structure even without a larger downstream theorem.
